requirements.requirement: Establish dual redundant transit paths (two /30 links) between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) carrying dynamic routing so traffic can be carried across either path
requirements.summary: Both transit subnets (10.10.1.0/30, 10.10.2.0/30) were addressed on node1/node2 and confirmed reachable (cmd-80ba2c9137584f67, cmd-c5ea9a8f0ee144d8). OSPF area 0.0.0.0 was configured natively on VyOS FRR and via os-frr/Quagga on OPNsense, with Full adjacency formed on both transit links from both routers and an ECMP route to the far private subnet installed via both next-hops (cmd-8bb68c98c840420e, cmd-94f10db9f19d4abe, cmd-62f03553e32f4f15, cmd-b92df274d0474c25).

requirements.requirement: Private hosts node3 (behind node1) and node4 (behind node2) reach each other end-to-end across the transit fabric
requirements.summary: Direct pings from node3 (10.10.10.10) to node4 (10.10.20.10) and vice versa succeeded with 0% loss after addressing and OSPF convergence.

requirements.requirement: Connectivity between node3 and node4 continues when transit network A is taken out of service, and is restored when it returns
requirements.summary: A continuous ping (0.3s interval) from node3 to node4 was running when VyOS eth1 (transit-A) was administratively disabled; log analysis showed zero gaps across all 66 then 117 continuous sequence numbers spanning the disable/re-enable transition, and OSPF neighbor/route state directly confirmed adjacency dropped to transit-B-only during the outage and returned to dual Full adjacency after restoration.

requirements.requirement: Connectivity between node3 and node4 continues when transit network B is taken out of service, and is restored when it returns
requirements.summary: A second continuous ping was running when OPNsense vtnet2 (transit-B) was taken down and later restored; only 1 packet was lost out of 147, with OSPF neighbor/route state directly showing reconvergence to transit-A alone during the outage and full dual-path adjacency restored afterward, demonstrating the required failover transition a second time on the other link.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (node1-node4): pre-restart baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Each node had a pre-restart boot identity captured (node1 boot_id 7668189d, node2 kern.boottime 06:25:39, node3 boot_id 6ab98831, node4 boot_id 225ffbf7), a native restart issued with acknowledgement (return before disconnect / connection-refused polling confirming downtime), a changed post-restart boot identity (91db428f, 06:40:28, f8a76314, f6fb5627 respectively, all corroborated by the fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshot), and recovered interface/routing/reachability state confirmed per node plus a final full-topology check showing Full OSPF adjacency on both transit links and successful node3<->node4 ping after all four restarts.

overall_summary: The executor built OSPF-based ECMP routing over both transit links between VyOS (node1) and OPNsense (node2) and directly demonstrated, twice, that node3<->node4 connectivity survives a bounded outage of either transit network with near-zero packet loss and automatic OSPF reconvergence, followed by full restoration on link return. All four nodes were also carried through the mandated one-at-a-time restart protocol with matching pre/post boot identities (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots) and confirmed post-restart recovery of routing and end-to-end reachability. A real rp_filter bug surfaced during the node1 restart cycle was root-caused with tcpdump and fixed rather than worked around blindly.
limitations: Node1's own post-restart OSPF/reachability recovery was not immediately clean — one neighbor briefly showed 2-Way/DROther and node1->node4 pings failed repeatedly until the rp_filter issue on node3/node4 was diagnosed and fixed; final state was confirmed healthy but the trace shows an extended troubleshooting period rather than an immediately smooth recovery.
Minor temp-file residue (python config scripts on node2, ping-log files on node3) was not explicitly cleaned up, though low-risk and likely cleared by subsequent reboots.

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all state-changing commands map directly to task outcomes: interface/OSPF/firewall configuration on node1/node2, IP/route/sysctl configuration on node3/node4, the four restarts, and the bounded ping/tcpdump diagnostics used to root-cause the rp_filter issue (tcpdump processes were explicitly killed with pkill/kill after use, e.g. cmd-cce23dda3158476e, cmd-f5f4cf6e693a4d02). The rp_filter sysctl change on node3/node4 (cmd-bb06065e87024a12, cmd-8b716b75b0ac4be4, cmd-5cfb2d18d18e4154) is a real, low-risk, narrowly-scoped fix persisted to /etc/sysctl.conf that was directly required to make ECMP-routed replies work, not an unrelated experiment. Minor residue: helper python scripts (/tmp/f.py, /tmp/f2.py, /tmp/f3.py on node2) and continuous-ping log files (/tmp/failover_ping.log, /tmp/failover_ping2.log on node3) were left in /tmp rather than explicitly removed, though these are low-risk and likely cleared by the subsequent reboots of both nodes.
